what: A MoMAA interview dated 1 March 2021 describes the studio as marking its tenth anniversary and planning the second Congo Biennale for September to October 2021. Three searches found no later dated activity and no statement of closure, and the Congo Biennale website shows an account suspension notice.

also.what: The Congo Biennale website shows only a hosting notice that the account has been suspended. It carries no date and says nothing about the studio.

what: The New Times reported on 9 June 2026 that artists from Inema Arts Center take part in the Soil & Water: Kigali Crossings programme at Nyandungu Eco-Park. The centre's own site states it is open daily and shows no dated programme.
quote: Rwandan artists, including those from Inema Arts Center, will also take part.

also.what: The home page says "Inema Arts Center is open daily" and lists weekly yoga and dance classes without dates. Its footer carries a 2026 copyright line.

what: KNUST announced on 27 February 2026 that the blaxTARLINES KUMASI collective was selected to exhibit in the International Exhibition of the 2026 Venice Biennale.
quote: has been selected to exhibit at the International Exhibition of the Venice Biennale 2026

also.what: An e-flux Education feature dated 6 October 2026 describes a visit to the blaxTARLINES base on the KNUST campus in Kumasi and follows its presentation in Venice.

what: e-flux published the Education feature Trains of thought: On educational practices crossing Venice on 6 October 2026. Its announcements page carries current museum announcements without printed dates.

also.what: The announcements page lists recent client announcements, among them Krist Gruijthuijsen appointed Director of the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam. The page prints no dates; file timestamps in its image links read November 2026.
